## H3K27me3 genome wide distribution analysis

We load the genome of Ostreococcus tauri and compute the length of its 
chromosomes. We determine the length of the largest chromosome and for technical 
reasons we reverse the vector of lengths. This will be used to represent 
graphically the genome wide distribution of H3K27me3. 

```{r load_genome}
library(seqinr)

ostta.genome <- read.fasta(file = "../ostta_genome/ostreococcus_tauri.fa",
                           seqtype = "DNA")
chr.lens <- sapply(X = getSequence(ostta.genome),FUN = length)

number.chrs <- length(getSequence(ostta.genome))
max.chr.len <- max(chr.lens)
chr.lens <- rev(chr.lens)
```

We load the H3K27me3 peaks identified in cultures grown under constant light at 20ºC. We represent each chromosome using a rectangle. Each H3K27me3 peak is 
represented in its precise genome location using a blue rectangle. 

```{r visualization of H3K27me3 genome wide distribution}
ll.20 <- read.table(file="h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_peaks.bed",
                       header = F)

ll.20 <- ll.20[,1:3]

nrow(ll.20)

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_genome_wide_distribution_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 900,height = 900)
#par(mar=c(0,0,0,0))
plot(x=c(0,max.chr.len), y=c(0,4*number.chrs), col = "white", 
     xlab = "", ylab = "", axes=F)  

for(i in 1:number.chrs)
{
 polygon(x = c(0, chr.lens[i], chr.lens[i], 0),   
         y = c(4*i+1, 4*i+1, 4*i-1, 4*i-1),    
         col = "white") 
}

for(i in 1:nrow(ll.20))
{
 current.chr <- ll.20[i,1]
 current.start <- ll.20[i,2]
 current.end <- ll.20[i,3]

 current.line <- (20:1)[current.chr]
 
 polygon(x = c(current.start, 
               current.end, 
               current.end, 
               current.start),   
         y = c(4*current.line+1, 
               4*current.line+1, 
               4*current.line-1, 
               4*current.line-1),    
         col = "blue",border="blue")
}
#dev.off()
```

We identified 948 genomic regions significantly occupied by H3K27me3 in the 
three different independent biological replicates. We compute the percentage of
the whole genome occupied by H3K27me3 and the percentage in each chromosome. A 
barplot is used to represent the percentage of H3K27me3 in each chromosome. 
Z-scores and p-values are computed for each chromosome. A gradient from white 
to blue is used to represent significance levels.  

```{r k27_in_chrs}
h3k27me3.peaks.len <- ll.20$V3 - ll.20$V2
sum(h3k27me3.peaks.len)/sum(chr.lens)
ll.20 <- cbind(ll.20,h3k27me3.peaks.len)
colnames(ll.20) <- c("chr","start","end","length")
head(ll.20)
number.of.h3k27.peaks.chr <- vector(mode = "numeric",length = 20)
peaks.len.chr <- vector(mode = "numeric",length = 20)

for(i in 1:20)
{
 number.of.h3k27.peaks.chr[i] <- nrow(subset(ll.20, chr == i))
 peaks.len.chr[i] <- sum(subset(ll.20, chr == i)[,4]) 
}

percentage.chr.k27 <- peaks.len.chr/rev(chr.lens)

z.scores <- (percentage.chr.k27 - mean(percentage.chr.k27))/sd(percentage.chr.k27)

which(z.scores > 2.5)

p.vals <- pnorm((percentage.chr.k27 - mean(percentage.chr.k27[-19]))/sd(percentage.chr.k27[-19]),lower.tail = F)

p.vals

values.for.colors <- round(-log10(p.vals)*40)
values.for.colors[19] <- 100

white.blue.palette <- colorRampPalette(c('white','blue'))

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_chr_barplot_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 1800,height = 900)
barplot(100*percentage.chr.k27,border="black",names.arg = paste0("Chr",1:20),las=2,col=white.blue.palette(100)[values.for.colors]
)
abline(h = 100*mean(percentage.chr.k27[-19]),lty=5)
#dev.off()
```

Approximately 15.2% of the Ostreococcus genome is occupied by H3K27me3. 
H3K27me3 is mostly uniformly distributed over the different chromosome although 
it significantly accumulates (p-value < 0.01) in Chr2 (sexual chromosome) and 
Chr19 (viral resistance chromosome) with p-values 6.5x10^-3^ and 2.24x10^-93^ 
respectively. 

We determine the gene features occupied by each H3K27me3 mark and the H3K27me3 
marked genes. 

```{r k27_peaks_annotation}
library(TxDb.Otauri.JGI)
txdb <- TxDb.Otauri.JGI

ostta.genes <- as.data.frame(genes(txdb))
head(ostta.genes)

target.genes <- vector(mode = "character",length = nrow(ll.20))
peak.annotation <- vector(mode = "character",length = nrow(ll.20))

for(i in 1:nrow(ll.20))
{
 current.chr <- ll.20[i,1]
 current.start <- ll.20[i,2]
 current.end <- ll.20[i,3]

 complete.gene.body <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                               start >= current.start & 
                               end <= current.end)
 
 overlap.tss.pos.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                              start >= current.start & start <= current.end & 
                              strand == "+")
 
 overlap.tss.neg.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                              end >= current.start & end <= current.end & 
                              strand == "-")
 
 overlap.tes.pos.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                              end >= current.start & end <= current.end & 
                              strand == "+")
 
 overlap.tes.neg.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                              start >= current.start & start <= current.end & 
                              strand == "-")

 inside.gene.body <- subset(ostta.genes, seqnames == current.chr & 
                             start <= current.start & end >= current.end)
 
 
 if(nrow(complete.gene.body) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(complete.gene.body$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "gene.body"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tss.pos.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tss.pos.strand$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TSS"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tss.neg.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tss.neg.strand$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TSS"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tes.pos.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tes.pos.strand$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TES"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tes.neg.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tes.neg.strand$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TES"
 } else if(nrow(inside.gene.body) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(inside.gene.body$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "internal.gene.body"
 } else
 {
  peak.annotation[i] <- "intergenic"
 }
}

freq.peak.annotation <- table(peak.annotation)
#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_pie_chart_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 900,height = 900)
#par(mar=c(0,0,0,0))
pie(freq.peak.annotation[c("gene.body",
                           "internal.gene.body",
                           "TSS", 
                           "TES",
                           "intergenic")],
    labels = c("Full Gene Body", 
               "Gene Body", 
               "TSS", 
               "TES", 
               "Intergenic"),
    clockwise = T,border = "black",col=c("blue","cyan","green","red","grey"))
#dev.off()

percentage.freq.peak.annotation <- 
  100*freq.peak.annotation/sum(freq.peak.annotation)


percentage.freq.peak.annotation["gene.body"] +
percentage.freq.peak.annotation["internal.gene.body"]

percentage.freq.peak.annotation

ll.20.peak.annotation <- cbind(ll.20[,1:3],
                               data.frame(peak.annotation,target.genes))

head(ll.20.peak.annotation)

write.table(x = ll.20.peak.annotation,
            file = "tables/H3K27me3_LL_20C_peak_annotation.tsv",
            quote = F,sep = "\t",row.names = F)

all.k27.genes <- unique(unlist(sapply(X =ll.20.peak.annotation$target.genes,
                                FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(all.k27.genes) <- NULL
length(all.k27.genes)
length(all.k27.genes)/7668
```
We found 475 genes associated to H3K27me3 marks corresponding to 6.2% of the 
entire Ostreococcus genome. H3K27me3 is mostly located occupying either the 
entire gene body (24.4%) or internal regions of gene body (43.2%). Although 
some regions occupied by H3K27me3 has been found overlapping only with the TSS 
(10.8%) or the TES (17.1%). H3K27me3 was found in intergenic regions only in 
4.5% of the cases. 

Next we use metageneplots to determine the shape of the H3K27me3 over its 
occupied genes. We consider three different sets of marked genes, genes with 
their entire gene body marked, genes with H3K27 inside their gene body with no 
overlap in the TSS or TES and genes with H3K27me3 overlapping their TSS or TES.

```{r k27_metageneplots}
## Function to compute ChIP signal over different tiles
ntile.signal <- function(signal.vector,number.tiles)
{
 step.len <- floor(length(signal.vector)/number.tiles)
 number.plus.1 <- length(signal.vector) %% number.tiles
 pos.plus.1 <- sort(sample(1:100,number.plus.1,replace = F))
 
 acum <- c(0)
 for(i in 1:number.tiles)
 {
  if(i %in% pos.plus.1)
  {
   acum <- c(acum,acum[i]+step.len+1)
  } else
  {
   acum <- c(acum,acum[i]+step.len)
  }
 }
 
 acum[1] <- 1
 
 n.tile.signal.vector <- vector(mode = "numeric",length = number.tiles)
 for(i in 2:length(acum))
 {
  n.tile.signal.vector[(i-1)] <- mean(signal.vector[acum[i-1]:acum[i]])
 }
 
 return(n.tile.signal.vector)
}

## Function to generate the data for a metageneplot
metageneplot <- function(gene.names,genes,bw.file.name,ntile.txs,ntile.gene.body)
{
 res <- matrix(nrow=length(gene.names),ncol=2*ntile.txs+ntile.gene.body)
 rownames(res) <- gene.names
 
 bw.file <- import.bw(con = bw.file.name)
 bw.file <- as.data.frame(bw.file)
 
 for(i in 1:length(gene.names))
 {
  #print(i)
  current.gene.chr <- genes[gene.names[i],"seqnames"]
  current.gene.start <- genes[gene.names[i],"start"]
  current.gene.end <- genes[gene.names[i],"end"]
  current.gene.strand <- genes[gene.names[i],"strand"]
  
  gene.body.signal <- subset(bw.file, seqnames == current.gene.chr & 
                              start >= current.gene.start & 
                              end <= current.gene.end)[["score"]]

  upstream.start.signal <- subset(bw.file, seqnames == current.gene.chr & 
                                   start >= (current.gene.start - 2000) & 
                                   end <= current.gene.start)[["score"]]
  
  downstream.end.signal <- subset(bw.file, seqnames == current.gene.chr & 
                                   start >= current.gene.end & 
                                   end <= (current.gene.end + 2000))[["score"]]
  
  ntile.signal.complete <- 
   c(ntile.signal(signal.vector = upstream.start.signal,number.tiles = ntile.txs),
     ntile.signal(signal.vector = gene.body.signal,number.tiles = ntile.gene.body),
     ntile.signal(signal.vector = downstream.end.signal,number.tiles = ntile.txs))
  
  if(current.gene.strand == "+")
  {
   res[i,] <- ntile.signal.complete
  } else
  {
   res[i,] <- rev(ntile.signal.complete)
  }
 }
 
 return(res)
}

## Genes with their entire gene body marked
k27.gene.body <- unique(unlist(sapply(
  X = subset(ll.20.peak.annotation, 
             peak.annotation == "gene.body")[["target.genes"]],
  FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k27.gene.body) <- NULL
length(k27.gene.body)

## Genes with H3K27 inside their gene body with no overlap
## in the TSS or TES.
k27.internal.gene.body <- unique(unlist(sapply(
  X = subset(ll.20.peak.annotation, 
             peak.annotation == "internal.gene.body")[["target.genes"]],
  FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k27.internal.gene.body) <- NULL
length(k27.internal.gene.body)

## Genes with H3K27me3 overlapping their TSS
k27.tss <- unique(unlist(sapply(
  X = subset(ll.20.peak.annotation, 
             peak.annotation == "TSS")[["target.genes"]],
  FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k27.tss) <- NULL
length(k27.tss)

## Genes with H3K27me3 overlapping their TES
k27.tes <- unique(unlist(sapply(
  X = subset(ll.20.peak.annotation, 
             peak.annotation == "TES")[["target.genes"]], 
  FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k27.tes) <- NULL
length(k27.tes)
```

Next we generate the metageneplots for genes where the H3K27me3 occupies their 
entire gene body including TSS and TES. 

```{r k27_metageneplots_gene_body}
library(rtracklayer)

metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.1 <- 
 metageneplot(gene.names = k27.gene.body,
              genes = ostta.genes,
              bw.file.name =
                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_chip_1.bw",
              ntile.txs = 10,
              ntile.gene.body = 20)
median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.1 <- 
 apply(X = metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.1,
      MARGIN = 2,
      FUN = median,na.rm = T)

metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.2 <- 
 metageneplot(gene.names = k27.gene.body,
              genes = ostta.genes,
              bw.file.name =
                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_chip_2.bw",
              ntile.txs = 10,
              ntile.gene.body = 20)
median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.2 <- 
 apply(X = metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.2,
      MARGIN = 2,
      FUN = median,na.rm = T)

metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.3 <- 
 metageneplot(gene.names = k27.gene.body,
              genes = ostta.genes,
              bw.file.name =
                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_chip_3.bw",
              ntile.txs = 10,
              ntile.gene.body = 20)
median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.3 <- 
 apply(X = metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.3,
      MARGIN = 2,
      FUN = median,na.rm = T)

median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body <- 
  (median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.1 + 
     median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.2 + 
     median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.3)/3

plot(smooth.spline(x=1:40,y=median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body,spar = 0.5),
     type="l",col="blue",lwd=3,ylim=c(0,45),axes=F,xlab="",ylab="")
axis(side = 1, at=c(0,10,30,40),labels = c("-2Kb","TSS","TES","2Kb"),
     las=2,lwd=2)
axis(side = 2,lwd=2)
```

In order to compare the different metageneplots are represented in the same plot.

```{r all_k27_metageneplots}

plot(smooth.spline(x=1:40,y=median.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body,spar = 0.5),
     type="l",col="blue",lwd=3,ylim=c(0,45),axes=F,xlab="",ylab="")
lines(smooth.spline(x=1:40,y=median.metageneplot.data.k27.internal.gene.body,
                    spar = 0.5),
      type="l",col="cyan",lwd=3)

      type="l",col="green",lwd=3)

     las=2,lwd=2)
```

It can be observed that the level of H3K27me3 mark varies depending on the part 
of gene that it occupies. Next we check if these differences are significant.  

```{r metageneplots_significance}
max.metageneplot.data.k27.gene.body.1 <-
```


We can see all H3K27me3 genes present levels of expression significantly lower 
than non-marked genes. Specifically, genes whose entire gene body or TSS is 
occupied by H3K27me3 are completely repressed. Whereas, genes where only the TES 
or gene body is occupied by H3K27me3 are expressed although at a significantly 
lower level than non-marked genes.  

In what follows we perform a functional analysis over the H3K27me3 marked genes. 
First, we analyze the relationship between H3K27me3 peaks and transposable 
elements. 

```{r transposable_elements}
dna.transposons <- 
  read.table(file="../te_analysis/dna_transposons_unsorted.bed",
             sep="\t",header=F)
nrow(dna.transposons)

ltr.transposons <- 
  read.table(file="../te_analysis/ltr_transposons_unsorted.bed",
             sep="\t", header=F)
nrow(ltr.transposons)

unclassified.transposons <- 
  read.table(file="../te_analysis/unknown_transposons_unsorted.bed", 
             sep="\t",header = F)
nrow(unclassified.transposons)

overlapping.peaks <- function(target.peak, peaks)
{
 subset(peaks, V1 == target.peak[1] & (
             (V2 >= target.peak[2] & V2 <= target.peak[3]) |
             (V3 >= target.peak[2] & V3 <= target.peak[3]) |
             (V2 <= target.peak[2] & V3 >= target.peak[3])))
}


peak.te <- vector(mode = "character",length = nrow(ll.20.peak.annotation))

for(i in 1:nrow(ll.20.peak.annotation))
{
 current.peak <- unlist(ll.20.peak.annotation[i,1:3])
 
 if(nrow(overlapping.peaks(current.peak,dna.transposons)) > 0)
 {
  peak.te[i] <- "DNA_transposon"
 } else if (nrow(overlapping.peaks(current.peak,ltr.transposons)) > 0)
 {
  peak.te[i] <- "LTR_transposon"
 } else if (nrow(overlapping.peaks(current.peak,unclassified.transposons)) > 0)
 {
  peak.te[i] <- "Unclassified_transposon"
 } else
 {
  peak.te[i] <- "No_transposon"
 }
}

100*table(peak.te)/sum(table(peak.te))

pie(table(peak.te), col=c("black","grey","white","lightblue"))

nrow(dna.transposons)
100*table(peak.te)["DNA_transposon"]/nrow(dna.transposons)

nrow(ltr.transposons)
100*table(peak.te)["LTR_transposon"]/nrow(ltr.transposons)

nrow(unclassified.transposons)
100*table(peak.te)["Unclassified_transposon"]/nrow(unclassified.transposons)


table(ll.20.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "DNA_transposon"])
table(ll.20.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "LTR_transposon"])
table(ll.20.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "Unclassified_transposon"])

table(ll.20.peak.annotation$peak.annotation)

(table(ll.20.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "DNA_transposon"])["intergenic"] +
table(ll.20.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "LTR_transposon"])["intergenic"] +
table(ll.20.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "Unclassified_transposon"])["intergenic"]) / table(ll.20.peak.annotation$peak.annotation)["intergenic"]

ll.20.peak.annotation <- cbind(ll.20.peak.annotation,peak.te)
write.table(x = ll.20.peak.annotation,file = "tables/H3K27me3_LL_20C_peak_annotation.tsv",quote = F,sep = "\t",row.names = F)
```

H3K27me3 is only partially associated with Transposable Elements. More than 84% 
of the peaks did not overlap with any TE. Only 1.5%, 0.5% and 13.5% of the 
H3K27me3 peaks were found overlapping with DNA, LTR and unclassified
transposons respectively. Most TE were neither associated with H3K27me3 peaks, 
specifically 14 out of 35 (40%) DNA transposons, 5 out of 69 (7.25%) LTR 
transposons and 128 out of 988 (13%) unclassified transposons were H3K27me3 
marked. Nonetheless, most H3K27me3 marks 
located at intergenic regions (74.42%) were associated with transposons.

Our GO enrichment analysis suggests that H3K27me3 is repressing the assembly of
bounded cellular projection, microtubule-based movement and transcription
regulation. Other processes are also significantly affected such as fatty acid 
metabolism and cell differentiation.

For example, the transcription factors ostta14g02090 (Arabidopsis ortholog 
APETALA2 AT4G36920), ostta17g00450 (Arabidopsis ortholog BELL1 AT5G41410),
ostta11g02490, ostta07g04340 (Arabidopsis orthologs WRKY AT2G04880) and 
ostta02g03030 (Arabidopsis ortholog CSP, cold shock protein, AT2G17870).

```{r function gene profile}
library(rtracklayer)  
library(ChIPpeakAnno)
 
genes.data.df <- as.data.frame(genes(txdb))
cds.data <- as.data.frame(cds(txdb))
exons.data <- as.data.frame(exons(txdb))

gene.profile <- function(gene.name, 
                         promoter_length=1000, 
                         selected.bigwig.files, 
                         selected.bed.files)
{
  target.gene.body <- genes.data.df[gene.name,]
  target.gene.chr <- as.character(target.gene.body$seqnames)
  target.gene.start <- target.gene.body$start
  target.gene.end <- target.gene.body$end
  
  target.gene.strand <- as.character(target.gene.body$strand)
  
  ## Extract cds annotation
  cds.data.target.gene <- subset(cds.data, 
                                 seqnames == target.gene.chr & 
                                   (start >= target.gene.start & 
                                      end <= target.gene.end))
  
  ## Extract exons annotation
  exons.data.target.gene <- subset(exons.data, 
                                   seqnames == target.gene.chr & 
                                     (start >= target.gene.start & 
                                        end <= target.gene.end))
  
  ## Determine the genome range to plot including promoter, gene body and 5' UTR
  ## This depends on whether the gene is on the forward or reverse strand
  range.to.plot <- target.gene.body
  
  if(target.gene.strand == "+")
  {
    range.to.plot$start <- range.to.plot$start - promoter_length
    range.to.plot$end <- range.to.plot$end + promoter_length
  } else if (target.gene.strand == "-")
  {
    range.to.plot$end <- range.to.plot$end + promoter_length
    range.to.plot$start <- range.to.plot$start - promoter_length
  }
  
  ## Compute the length of the genome range to represent
  current.length <- range.to.plot$end - range.to.plot$start
  
  ## Compute profile in gene
  ## Since ChIPpeakAnno needs more than one region to plot our region
  ## is duplicated 
  regions.plot <- GRanges(rbind(range.to.plot,range.to.plot))
  
  ## Import signal from the bigwig files
  cvglists <- sapply(selected.bigwig.files, import, 
                     format="BigWig", 
                     which=regions.plot, 
                     as="RleList")
  
  ## Compute signal in the region to plot
  chip.signal <- featureAlignedSignal(cvglists, regions.plot, 
                                      upstream=ceiling(current.length/2), 
                                      downstream=ceiling(current.length/2),
                                      n.tile=current.length) 
  
  ## Compute mean signal 
  if(target.gene.strand == "+")
  {
    chip.signal.mean <- colMeans(chip.signal[[1]],na.rm = TRUE)
  } else if (target.gene.strand == "-")
  {
    chip.signal.mean <- rev(colMeans(chip.signal[[1]],na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  
  ## Normalization
  #chip.signal.mean <- 20 * chip.signal.mean / max(chip.signal.mean)
  upper.lim <- 1.1*max(chip.signal.mean)
  ## Colors to draw signal
  line.colors <- "blue"
  area.colors <- "lightblue"
  
  gene.height <- -25
  cord.x <- 1:current.length
  
  ## Exon width to plot
  exon.width <- 2#1#2
  
  ## Cds width to plot
  cds.width <- 3#1.5#3
  
  ## Width of the rectangule representing the peak reagion
  peak.width <- 1#0.5#1
  
  ## Extract exons for target gene
  exons.data.target.gene <- subset(exons.data, seqnames == target.gene.chr & (start >= target.gene.start & end <= target.gene.end))
  
  ## Transform exon coordinates to current range
  min.pos <- min(exons.data.target.gene$start)
  
  exons.data.target.gene$start <- exons.data.target.gene$start - min.pos + promoter_length
  exons.data.target.gene$end <- exons.data.target.gene$end - min.pos + promoter_length
  
  ## Extract cds for target gene
  cds.data.target.gene <- subset(cds.data, seqnames == target.gene.chr & (start >= target.gene.start & end <= target.gene.end))
  
  cds.data.target.gene$start <- cds.data.target.gene$start - min.pos + promoter_length
  cds.data.target.gene$end <- cds.data.target.gene$end - min.pos + promoter_length
  
  plot(cord.x, rep(gene.height,length(cord.x)),type="l",col="black",lwd=3,ylab="",
       cex.lab=2,axes=FALSE,xlab="",main="",cex.main=2,
       ylim=c(-35,upper.lim),xlim=c(0,max(cord.x)))
  
  ## Represent exons
  for(i in 1:nrow(exons.data.target.gene))
  {
    # Determine start/end for each exon
    current.exon.start <- exons.data.target.gene$start[i]
    current.exon.end <- exons.data.target.gene$end[i]
    
    ## Determine coordinates for each exon polygon and represent it
    exon.x <- c(current.exon.start,current.exon.end,current.exon.end,current.exon.start)
    exon.y <- c(gene.height + exon.width, gene.height + exon.width, gene.height - exon.width, gene.height - exon.width)
    
    polygon(x = exon.x, y = exon.y, col = "blue",border = "blue")
  }
  
  if(nrow(cds.data.target.gene) > 0)
  {
    for(i in 1:nrow(cds.data.target.gene))
    {
      # Determine current cds start/end
      current.cds.start <- cds.data.target.gene$start[i]
      current.cds.end <- cds.data.target.gene$end[i]
      
      # Determine curret cds coordinates for the polygon and represent it
      cds.x <- c(current.cds.start,current.cds.end,current.cds.end,current.cds.start)
      cds.y <- c(gene.height + cds.width, gene.height + cds.width, gene.height - cds.width, gene.height - cds.width)
      polygon(x = cds.x, y = cds.y, col = "blue",border = "blue")
    }
  }
  
  ## Draw arrow to represent transcription direction 
  if(target.gene.strand == "+")
  {
    lines(c(promoter_length,promoter_length,promoter_length+100),
          y=c(gene.height,gene.height+5,gene.height+5),lwd=3)
    lines(c(promoter_length+50,promoter_length+100),y=c(gene.height+6,gene.height+5),lwd=3)
    lines(c(promoter_length+50,promoter_length+100),y=c(gene.height+4,gene.height+5),lwd=3)
  } else if (target.gene.strand == "-")
  {
    lines(c(current.length - promoter_length, current.length - promoter_length, current.length - promoter_length-100),y=c(gene.height,gene.height+5,gene.height+5),lwd=3)
    lines(c(current.length - promoter_length-50, current.length - promoter_length - 100),y=c(gene.height + 6, gene.height + 5),lwd=3)
    lines(c(current.length - promoter_length-50, current.length - promoter_length - 100),y=c(gene.height + 4, gene.height + 5),lwd=3)
  }
  
  ## Draw promoter range
  if(target.gene.strand == "+")
  {
    axis(side = 1,labels = c(- promoter_length, - promoter_length / 2,"TSS"),at = c(1,promoter_length/2,promoter_length),lwd=2,cex=1.5,las=2,cex=2)
  } else if(target.gene.strand == "-")
  {
    axis(side = 1,labels = c("TSS",- promoter_length / 2,- promoter_length),at = c(current.length-promoter_length,current.length-promoter_length/2, current.length),lwd=2,cex=1.5,las=2,cex=2)
  }
  
  ## Draw gene name
  text(x = current.length / 2, y = -33 , 
       labels = bquote(italic(.(gene.name))),cex = 1.7,font = 3)
  
  ## Extract bed file name 1 and read it
  current.peaks <- read.table(file=selected.bed.files,header = F, as.is = T)
  current.peaks <- current.peaks[,1:3]
  colnames(current.peaks) <- c("seqnames","start","end")
  peak.coordinates <- subset(current.peaks, seqnames == as.character(range.to.plot$seqnames) & start >= range.to.plot$start & end <= range.to.plot$end) 
  current.peaks.to.plot <- peak.coordinates[,2:3]
  
  ## Transform coordinates 
  current.peaks.to.plot <- current.peaks.to.plot - range.to.plot$start
  
  ## Check if there are peaks for the target gene
  if(nrow(current.peaks.to.plot) > 0)
  {
    #motifs.in.peaks <- vector(mode="list", length=nrow(current.peaks.to.plot))
    for(j in 1:nrow(current.peaks.to.plot))
    {
      ## Extract start and end point of each peak region
      current.peak.start <- current.peaks.to.plot[j,1]
      current.peak.end <- current.peaks.to.plot[j,2]
      
      ## Computer coordinates for polygon and draw it
      peak.x <- c(current.peak.start,current.peak.end,
                  current.peak.end,current.peak.start)
      peak.y <- c(peak.width - 12,   peak.width - 12, 
                  - peak.width - 12, - peak.width - 12)  
      
      polygon(x = peak.x, y = peak.y, col = "blue", border = "blue",lwd=2)
    }
  }
  
  ## Draw profiles if bw file is provided
  ## Compute base line for current TF
  current.base.line <- - 10
  
  ## Represent signal from the current TF
  lines(chip.signal.mean+current.base.line,type="l",col=line.colors,lwd=3)
  ## Determine polygon coordinates and represent it
  cord.y <- c(current.base.line,chip.signal.mean+current.base.line,current.base.line)
  cord.x <- 1:length(cord.y)
  polygon(cord.x,cord.y,col=area.colors)
  
  axis(side = 2,lwd = 2,
       at = seq(from=0,to=ceiling(upper.lim/10)*10,by=10)+current.base.line,
       labels = seq(from=0,to=ceiling(upper.lim/10)*10,by=10))
}

#jpeg(filename = "images/example_ostta14g02090.jpg",res = 250,width = 3800,height = 1500)

             promoter_length=1000, 
             selected.bigwig.files="h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_chip_1.bw", 
             selected.bed.files="h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_peaks.bed")

#dev.off()

#dev.off()
```

```{r microtubule_movement}
gene.profile(gene.name="ostta18g01040",
```

We next explore the association between ChIP signal and gene expression. The
Reads Per Kilobase of peak and Million of mapped reads (RPKM) is computed. 
Marked genes with different levels of ChIP signal according to the quantiles
of the distribution are separated into different sets adn their expression 
level represented. 

```{r chip_signal_vs_expression}
count.1 <- 
  read.table(
    file = 
      "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_chip_1_counts.bed",
      #"../chipseq_data/bed_data/h3k27me3/temp20c/k27_20_ll_chip_1_counts.bed",
    header = F,sep = "\t")
count.2 <- 
  read.table(
    file=
      "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_chip_2_counts.bed",
      #"../chipseq_data/bed_data/h3k27me3/temp20c/k27_20_ll_chip_2n_counts.bed",
    header = F,sep = "\t")
count.3 <- 
  read.table(
    file=
      "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_20_chip_3_counts.bed",
      #"../chipseq_data/bed_data/h3k27me3/temp20c/k27_20_ll_chip_3n_counts.bed",
    header = F,sep = "\t")
#count.1 <- count.1[,c(1:3,10)]
#count.2 <- count.2[,c(1:3,10)]
#count.3 <- count.3[,c(1:3,10)]

mapped.reads.k27.20c.1 <- 3146662/1E6 
mapped.reads.k27.20c.2 <- 7702115/1E6
mapped.reads.k27.20c.3 <- 7102648/1E6

rpm.1 <- count.1
rpm.2 <- count.2
rpm.3 <- count.3

rpm.1[,4] <- rpm.1[,4]/mapped.reads.k27.20c.1
rpm.2[,4] <- rpm.2[,4]/mapped.reads.k27.20c.2
rpm.3[,4] <- rpm.3[,4]/mapped.reads.k27.20c.3


plot(log2(rpm.1[,4]),log2(rpm.2[,4]))
lines(x=c(0,100),y=c(0,100))

plot(log2(rpm.1[,4]),log2(rpm.3[,4]))
lines(x=c(0,100),y=c(0,100))

plot(log2(rpm.2[,4]),log2(rpm.3[,4]))
lines(x=c(0,100),y=c(0,100))

rpm <- rpm.1
rpm[,4] <- (rpm.1[,4] + rpm.2[,4] + rpm.3[,4])/3

rpkm <- rpm
rpkm[,4] <- (rpm[,4]/(rpm[,3]-rpm[,2]))

genes.2nd.quant <- 
  (ll.20.peak.annotation$target.genes)[which(rpkm[,4] < quantile(rpkm[,4])[3])]
genes.2nd.quant <- genes.2nd.quant[genes.2nd.quant != ""]
genes.2nd.quant <- unlist(strsplit(x = genes.2nd.quant,split = ","))

genes.3rd.quant <- 
  ll.20.peak.annotation$target.genes[which(rpkm[,4] >= quantile(rpkm[,4])[3] &
                                           rpkm[,4] < quantile(rpkm[,4])[4])]
genes.3rd.quant <- genes.3rd.quant[genes.3rd.quant != ""]
genes.3rd.quant <- unlist(strsplit(x = genes.3rd.quant,split = ","))

genes.4th.quant <- 
  ll.20.peak.annotation$target.genes[which(rpkm[,4] >= quantile(rpkm[,4])[4])]
genes.4th.quant <- genes.4th.quant[genes.4th.quant != ""]
genes.4th.quant <- unlist(strsplit(x = genes.4th.quant,split = ","))

##jpeg(filename = "../images/boxplot_chip_signal_gene_expression.jpg",width = 400,height = 600)
boxplot(gene.expression.20[genes.2nd.quant],
        gene.expression.20[genes.3rd.quant],
        gene.expression.20[genes.4th.quant],
        names=c("RPKM < 0.3","0.3 < RPKM < 0.5", "RPKM > 0.5"),
        ylab="TPM", cex.lab=1.5, outline=F, col=c("lightblue","blue","darkblue"))
##dev.off()

boxplot(gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.gene.body,genes.2nd.quant)],
        gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.gene.body,genes.3rd.quant)],
        gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.gene.body,genes.4th.quant)],
        names=c("< 0.3","< 0.5", "> 0.5"),outline=F)

boxplot(gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.tss,genes.2nd.quant)],
        gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.tss,genes.3rd.quant)],
        gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.tss,genes.4th.quant)],
        names=c("< 0.3","< 0.5", "> 0.5"),outline=F)

boxplot(gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.tes,genes.2nd.quant)],
        gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.tes,genes.3rd.quant)],
        gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.tes,genes.4th.quant)],
        names=c("< 0.3","< 0.5", "> 0.5"),outline=F)

boxplot(gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.internal.gene.body,genes.2nd.quant)],
        gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.internal.gene.body,genes.3rd.quant)],
        gene.expression.20[intersect(k27.internal.gene.body,genes.4th.quant)],
        names=c("< 0.3","< 0.5", "> 0.5"),outline=F)
```

## H3K4me3 genome wide distribution analysis

We load the H3K4me3 peaks identified in cultures grown under constant light at 20ºC. We represent each chromosome using a rectangle. Each H3K4me3 peak is represented in its precise genome location using a dark orange rectangle. 


```{r visualization of H3K4me3 genome wide distribution}
k4.ll.20 <- read.table(file="chipseq_data/bed_data/h3k4me3/h3k4me3_ll_20.bed",
                       header = F)

k4.ll.20 <- k4.ll.20[,1:3]

nrow(k4.ll.20)

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_genome_wide_distribution_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 900,height = 900)
#par(mar=c(0,0,0,0))
plot(x=c(0,max.chr.len), y=c(0,4*number.chrs), col = "white", xlab = "", ylab = "", axes=F)  

for(i in 1:number.chrs)
{
 polygon(x = c(0, chr.lens[i], chr.lens[i], 0),   
         y = c(4*i+1, 4*i+1, 4*i-1, 4*i-1),    
         col = "white") 
}

for(i in 1:nrow(k4.ll.20))
{
 current.chr <- k4.ll.20[i,1]
 current.start <- k4.ll.20[i,2]
 current.end <- k4.ll.20[i,3]

 current.line <- (20:1)[current.chr]
 
 polygon(x = c(current.start, current.end, current.end, current.start),   
         y = c(4*current.line+1, 4*current.line+1, 4*current.line-1, 4*current.line-1),    
         col = "orange",border="orange")
}
#dev.off()
```
We identified 773 genomic regions significantly occupied by H3K4me3 in the three different independent biological replicates. We compute the percentage of the whole genome occupied by H3K4me3 and the percentage in each chromosome. A barplot is used to represent the percentage of H3K4me3 in each chromosome. Z-scores and p-values are computed for each chromosome. A gradient from white to dark orange is used to represent significance levels.  

```{r k4_in_chrs}
h3k4me3.peaks.len <- k4.ll.20$V3 - k4.ll.20$V2
sum(h3k4me3.peaks.len)/sum(chr.lens)
k4.ll.20 <- cbind(k4.ll.20,h3k4me3.peaks.len)
colnames(k4.ll.20) <- c("chr","start","end","length")
head(k4.ll.20)
number.of.h3k4.peaks.chr <- vector(mode = "numeric",length = 20)
k4.peaks.len.chr <- vector(mode = "numeric",length = 20)

for(i in 1:20)
{
 number.of.h3k4.peaks.chr[i] <- nrow(subset(k4.ll.20, chr == i))
 k4.peaks.len.chr[i] <- sum(subset(k4.ll.20, chr == i)[,4]) 
}

percentage.chr.k4 <- k4.peaks.len.chr/rev(chr.lens)

k4.z.scores <- (percentage.chr.k4 - mean(percentage.chr.k4))/sd(percentage.chr.k4)

which(k4.z.scores > 2.5)
which(k4.z.scores < -2.5)

p.vals <- pnorm((percentage.chr.k4 - mean(percentage.chr.k4[-20]))/sd(percentage.chr.k4[-20]),lower.tail = F)

p.vals

values.for.colors <- round(-log10(p.vals)*40+1)
values.for.colors[20] <- 100

white.darkorange.palette <- colorRampPalette(c('white','darkorange'))

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_chr_barplot_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 1800,height = 900)
barplot(100*percentage.chr.k4,border="black",names.arg = paste0("Chr",1:20),las=2,col=white.darkorange.palette(100)[values.for.colors]
)
abline(h = 100*mean(percentage.chr.k4[-20]),lty=5)
#dev.off()
```
Approximately 3.7% of the Ostreococcus genome is occupied by H3K4me3. 
H3K4me3 is mostly uniformly distributed over the different chromosome although it significantly accumulates (p-value < 0.01) in Chr20 with p-value 5.32x10^-4^.

We determine the gene features occupied by each H3K4me3 mark and the H3K4me3 marked genes. 

```{r k4_peaks_annotation}
library(TxDb.Otauri.JGI)
txdb <- TxDb.Otauri.JGI

ostta.genes <- as.data.frame(genes(txdb))
head(ostta.genes)

target.genes <- vector(mode = "character",length = nrow(k4.ll.20))
peak.annotation <- vector(mode = "character",length = nrow(k4.ll.20))

for(i in 1:nrow(k4.ll.20))
{
 current.chr <- k4.ll.20[i,1]
 current.start <- k4.ll.20[i,2]
 current.end <- k4.ll.20[i,3]
 
 complete.gene.body <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                               start >= current.start & 
                               end <= current.end)
 
 overlap.tss.pos.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                                  seqnames == current.chr & 
                                   start >= current.start & start <= current.end & 
                                   strand == "+")
 
 overlap.tss.neg.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                                  seqnames == current.chr & 
                                   end >= current.start & end <= current.end & 
                                   strand == "-")
 
 overlap.tes.pos.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                                  seqnames == current.chr & 
                                   end >= current.start & end <= current.end & 
                                   strand == "+")
 
 overlap.tes.neg.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                                  seqnames == current.chr & 
                                   start >= current.start & start <= current.end & 
                                   strand == "-")
 
 inside.gene.body <- subset(ostta.genes, seqnames == current.chr & 
                             start <= current.start & end >= current.end)
 
 
 if(nrow(complete.gene.body) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(complete.gene.body$gene_id),collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "gene.body"
 } else if((nrow(overlap.tss.pos.strand) > 0) | (nrow(overlap.tss.neg.strand) > 0))
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(c(unlist(overlap.tss.pos.strand$gene_id),
                             unlist(overlap.tss.neg.strand$gene_id)),collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TSS"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tes.pos.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tes.pos.strand$gene_id),collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TES"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tes.neg.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tes.neg.strand$gene_id),collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TES"
 } else if(nrow(inside.gene.body) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(inside.gene.body$gene_id),collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "internal.gene.body"
 } else
 {
  peak.annotation[i] <- "intergenic"
 }
}

freq.peak.annotation <- table(peak.annotation)
#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k4me3_pie_chart_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 900,height = 900)
#par(mar=c(0,0,0,0))
pie(freq.peak.annotation[c("gene.body",
                           "internal.gene.body",
                           "TSS", 
                           "TES",
                           "intergenic")],
    labels = c("Full Gene Body", 
               "Gene Body", 
               "TSS", 
               "TES", 
               "Intergenic"),
    clockwise = T,border = "black",col=c("blue","cyan","green","red","grey"))
#dev.off()

percentage.freq.peak.annotation <- 100*freq.peak.annotation/sum(freq.peak.annotation)

percentage.freq.peak.annotation

k4.ll.20.peak.annotation <- cbind(k4.ll.20[,1:3],data.frame(peak.annotation,target.genes))

head(k4.ll.20.peak.annotation)

write.table(x = k4.ll.20.peak.annotation,file = "tables/H3K4me3_LL_20C_peak_annotation.tsv",quote = F,sep = "\t",row.names = F)

all.k4.genes <- (unlist(sapply(X =k4.ll.20.peak.annotation$target.genes,
                                FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(all.k4.genes) <- NULL
length(all.k4.genes)
length(all.k4.genes)/7668
```

We found 832 genes associated to H3K4me3 marks corresponding to 10.9% of the entire Ostreococcus genome. H3K4me3 is mostly located occupying the TSS (78.4%) with marginal percentages for internal regions of gene body (8.2%), intergenic regions (7%), entire gene bodies (5.3%) and TES (1.2%).  

Next we use metageneplots to determine the shape of the H3K27me3 over its occupied genes. We consider three different sets of marked genes, genes with their entire gene body marked, genes with H3K27 inside their gene body with no overlap in the TSS or TES and genes with H3K27me3 overlapping their TSS or TES

Next we generate the metageneplots for genes where the H3K27me3 occupies their entire gene body including TSS and TES. 

```{r k4_metageneplots_gene_body}
library(rtracklayer)
## Genes with their entire gene body marked
k4.gene.body <- (unlist(sapply(X = subset(k4.ll.20.peak.annotation, 
                                          peak.annotation == "gene.body")[["target.genes"]],
                                FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))

length(k4.gene.body)

## Genes with H3K27 inside their gene body with no overlap

                          FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))

                          FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k4.tes) <- NULL
length(k4.tes)

metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body.1 <-

median.metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body.2 <-

metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body.3 <- 
 metageneplot(gene.names = k4.gene.body,
              genes = ostta.genes,
              bw.file.name = "chipseq_data/bw_data/h3k4me3/temp20/h3k4me3_20_chip_3.bw",
              ntile.txs = 10,
              ntile.gene.body = 20)
median.metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body.3 <- 
 apply(X = metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body.3,

       FUN = median,na.rm = T)

median.metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body <- (median.metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body.1 + 
                                           median.metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body.2 + 
                                           median.metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body.3)/3

plot(smooth.spline(x=1:40,y=median.metageneplot.data.k4.gene.body,spar = 0.5),
     type="l",col="blue",lwd=3,ylim=c(0,70),axes=F,xlab="",ylab="")
axis(side = 1, at=c(0,10,30,40),labels = c("-2Kb","TSS","TES","2Kb"),las=2,lwd=2)
axis(side = 2,lwd=2)
```


We can see all H3K4me3 genes present levels of expression significantly higher than non-marked genes. Specifically, genes whose entire gene body or TSS is occupied by H3K4me3 are much higher expressed. Whereas, genes where only the TES or gene body is occupied by H3K4me3 are expressed at a significantly higher level than non-marked genes but with much lower significance level.

## H3K27me3 and H3K4me3 common marked genes

The set of H3K27me3 and H3K4me3 genes only overlapped marginally. 

```{r venn_diagram_k27_k4}
overlap.k4.k27 <- read.table(file="chipseq_data/bed_data/h3k27me3_h3k4me3_ll_20.bed",header=F,sep = "\t",as.is = T)

max(overlap.k4.k27$V3 - overlap.k4.k27$V2)
summary(overlap.k4.k27$V3 - overlap.k4.k27$V2)
nrow(overlap.k4.k27)

library(VennDiagram)

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_h3k4me3_venndiagram.jpg",res = 250,width = 1500,height = 1500)
grid.newpage()
draw.pairwise.venn(area1 = length(all.k27.genes),cat.pos = c(180,180),cat.dist = 0.05,
                   area2 = length(all.k4.genes),
                   cross.area = length(intersect(all.k27.genes,all.k4.genes)),
                   lwd = 3,category = c("H3K27me3","H3K4me3"),euler.d = T,
                   col = c("blue","darkorange"),
                   fill = c(" blue","darkorange"),alpha = 0.5,
                   cex = 2,
                   cat.cex = 2)
#dev.off()
```

Only 19 genomic regions were found simultaneously marked by H3K27me3 and H3K4me3. The length of the overlap was never longer than 400bp and on average was less than 200bp. Taking into account that the length of DNA wrapped around a single nucleosome is approximately 150bp, no more than one or two nucleosomes appeared marked simultaneously by H3K27me3 and H3K4me3. 

Only 37 genes were identified as bivalent simultaneously marked with H3K27me3 and H3K4me3. Next we explore the positioning of these two marks in these genes and their level of expresssion.

```{r bivalent_marks_positioning}
k4.k27.genes <- intersect(all.k4.genes, all.k27.genes)
k4.k27.gene.annotation <- subset(ll.20.peak.annotation, target.genes %in% k4.k27.genes)
100*table(k4.k27.gene.annotation[!duplicated(k4.k27.gene.annotation$target.genes),][["peak.annotation"]])/nrow(k4.k27.gene.annotation)
```

In most bivalent genes H3K27me3 is located in inner regions of gene bodies (58.5%). In 14.6% of the bivalent genes H3K27me3 is located only at the TES. Whereas in only 9.8% and 4.9% H3K27me3 occupies the entire gene body or only the TSS, respectively. 


```{r bivalent_gene_expression}
non.k4.k27.genes <- intersect(non.k4.genes,non.k27.genes)
summary(gene.expression.20[all.k4.genes])
summary(gene.expression.20[all.k27.genes])
summary(gene.expression.20[k4.k27.genes])
summary(gene.expression.20[non.k4.k27.genes])

#jpeg(filename = "images/bivalent_expression_barplot.jpg",res = 250,width = 600,height = 1000)
boxplot(gene.expression.20[all.k27.genes],
        gene.expression.20[non.k4.k27.genes],
        gene.expression.20[k4.k27.genes],
        gene.expression.20[all.k4.genes],
        col=c("blue","grey",colorRampPalette(c('blue','darkorange'))(3)[2],"darkorange"),outline=F)
#dev.off()

wilcox.test(x = gene.expression.20[k4.k27.genes], y = gene.expression.20[non.k4.k27.genes])
wilcox.test(x = gene.expression.20[all.k27.genes], y = gene.expression.20[k4.k27.genes],alternative = "less")
wilcox.test(x = gene.expression.20[k4.k27.genes], y = gene.expression.20[all.k4.genes],alternative = "less")
```


## H3K27me3 consensus peaks covering different temperatures

We determined the genome wide distribution of H3K27me3 under different 
temperatures, 10ºC, 14ºC, 20ºC and 26ºC. We found differences as a response to
temperature. In order to compare H3K27me3 marks under different temperature we
merge all the peaks detected consistently in the three replicates for each 
temperature to generate a set of consensus peaks. Next we analyze the genome
wide distribution of the consensus H3K27me3 peaks.

```{r visualization of H3K27me3 genome wide distribution over different temps}
k27.consensus <- read.table(file="h3k27me3/h3k27me3_peaks.bed",
                       header = F)

nrow(k27.consensus)

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_genome_wide_distribution_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 900,height = 900)
#par(mar=c(0,0,0,0))
plot(x=c(0,max.chr.len), y=c(0,4*number.chrs), col = "white", 
     xlab = "", ylab = "", axes=F)  

for(i in 1:number.chrs)
{
 polygon(x = c(0, chr.lens[i], chr.lens[i], 0),   
         y = c(4*i+1, 4*i+1, 4*i-1, 4*i-1),    
         col = "white") 
}

for(i in 1:nrow(k27.consensus))
{
 current.chr <- k27.consensus[i,1]
 current.start <- k27.consensus[i,2]
 current.end <- k27.consensus[i,3]

 current.line <- (20:1)[current.chr]
 
 polygon(x = c(current.start, 
               current.end, 
               current.end, 
               current.start),   
         y = c(4*current.line+1, 
               4*current.line+1, 
               4*current.line-1, 
               4*current.line-1),    
         col = "blue",border="blue")
}
#dev.off()
```

We identified 1056 genomic regions significantly occupied by H3K27me3 in the 
three different  biological replicates at 10ºC, 14ºC, 20ºC or 26ºC. We compute 
the percentage of the whole genome occupied by H3K27me3 and the percentage in 
each chromosome. A  barplot is used to represent the percentage of H3K27me3 in 
each chromosome.  Z-scores and p-independentvalues are computed for each 
chromosome. A gradient from white to blue is used to represent significance 
levels.  

```{r k27_in_chrs consensus}
h3k27me3.peaks.len <- k27.consensus$V3 - k27.consensus$V2
sum(h3k27me3.peaks.len)/sum(chr.lens)
k27.consensus <- cbind(k27.consensus,h3k27me3.peaks.len)
colnames(k27.consensus) <- c("chr","start","end","length")
head(k27.consensus)
number.of.h3k27.peaks.chr <- vector(mode = "numeric",length = 20)
peaks.len.chr <- vector(mode = "numeric",length = 20)

for(i in 1:20)
{
 number.of.h3k27.peaks.chr[i] <- nrow(subset(k27.consensus, chr == i))
 peaks.len.chr[i] <- sum(subset(k27.consensus, chr == i)[,4]) 
}

percentage.chr.k27 <- peaks.len.chr/rev(chr.lens)

z.scores <- (percentage.chr.k27 - mean(percentage.chr.k27))/sd(percentage.chr.k27)

which(z.scores > 2.5)

p.vals <- pnorm((percentage.chr.k27 - mean(percentage.chr.k27[-19]))/sd(percentage.chr.k27[-19]),lower.tail = F)

p.vals

values.for.colors <- round(-log10(p.vals)*40)
values.for.colors[19] <- 100

white.blue.palette <- colorRampPalette(c('white','blue'))

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_chr_barplot_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 1800,height = 900)
barplot(100*percentage.chr.k27,border="black",names.arg = paste0("Chr",1:20),las=2,col=white.blue.palette(100)[values.for.colors]
)
abline(h = 100*mean(percentage.chr.k27[-19]),lty=5)
#dev.off()
```

Approximately 14.5% of the Ostreococcus genome is occupied by H3K27me3. 
H3K27me3 is mostly uniformly distributed over the different chromosome although 
it significantly accumulates (p-value < 0.01) in Chr2 (sexual chromosome), Chr16
and Chr19 (viral resistance chromosome) with p-values 1.58x10^-2^, 3.36x10^-2^ 
and 4.05x10^-39^respectively. 

We determine the gene features occupied by each H3K27me3 mark and the H3K27me3 
marked genes. 

```{r k27_peaks_annotation consensus}
library(TxDb.Otauri.JGI)
txdb <- TxDb.Otauri.JGI

ostta.genes <- as.data.frame(genes(txdb))
head(ostta.genes)

target.genes <- vector(mode = "character",length = nrow(k27.consensus))
peak.annotation <- vector(mode = "character",length = nrow(k27.consensus))

for(i in 1:nrow(k27.consensus))
{
 current.chr <- k27.consensus[i,1]
 current.start <- k27.consensus[i,2]
 current.end <- k27.consensus[i,3]

 complete.gene.body <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                               start >= current.start & 
                               end <= current.end)
 
 overlap.tss.pos.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                              start >= current.start & start <= current.end & 
                              strand == "+")
 
 overlap.tss.neg.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                              end >= current.start & end <= current.end & 
                              strand == "-")
 
 overlap.tes.pos.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                              end >= current.start & end <= current.end & 
                              strand == "+")
 
 overlap.tes.neg.strand <- subset(ostta.genes, 
                              seqnames == current.chr & 
                              start >= current.start & start <= current.end & 
                              strand == "-")

 inside.gene.body <- subset(ostta.genes, seqnames == current.chr & 
                             start <= current.start & end >= current.end)
 
 
 if(nrow(complete.gene.body) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(complete.gene.body$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "gene.body"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tss.pos.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tss.pos.strand$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TSS"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tss.neg.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tss.neg.strand$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TSS"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tes.pos.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tes.pos.strand$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TES"
 } else if(nrow(overlap.tes.neg.strand) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(overlap.tes.neg.strand$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "TES"
 } else if(nrow(inside.gene.body) > 0)
 {
  target.genes[i] <- paste(unlist(inside.gene.body$gene_id),
                           collapse = ",")
  peak.annotation[i] <- "internal.gene.body"
 } else
 {
  peak.annotation[i] <- "intergenic"
 }
}

freq.peak.annotation <- table(peak.annotation)
#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_pie_chart_ll_20.jpg",res = 300,width = 900,height = 900)
#par(mar=c(0,0,0,0))
pie(freq.peak.annotation[c("gene.body",
                           "internal.gene.body",
                           "TSS", 
                           "TES",
                           "intergenic")],
    labels = c("Full Gene Body", 
               "Gene Body", 
               "TSS", 
               "TES", 
               "Intergenic"),
    clockwise = T,border = "black",col=c("blue","cyan","green","red","grey"))
#dev.off()

percentage.freq.peak.annotation <- 
  100*freq.peak.annotation/sum(freq.peak.annotation)


percentage.freq.peak.annotation["gene.body"] +
percentage.freq.peak.annotation["internal.gene.body"]

percentage.freq.peak.annotation

k27.consensus.peak.annotation <- cbind(k27.consensus[,1:3],
                               data.frame(peak.annotation,target.genes))

rownames(k27.consensus.peak.annotation) <- apply(X = k27.consensus.peak.annotation[,1:3],
      MARGIN = 1,
      FUN = 
        function(x)
        {
          paste(x[1],paste(x[2],x[3],sep="-"),sep=":")
        })

head(k27.consensus.peak.annotation)

write.table(x = k27.consensus.peak.annotation,
            file = "tables/H3K27me3_consensus_peak_annotation.tsv",
            quote = F,sep = "\t",row.names = F)

all.k27.genes <- unique(unlist(sapply(X =k27.consensus.peak.annotation$target.genes,
                                FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(all.k27.genes) <- NULL
length(all.k27.genes)
length(all.k27.genes)/7668

## Genes with their entire gene body marked
k27.gene.body <- unique(unlist(sapply(
  X = subset(k27.consensus.peak.annotation, 
             peak.annotation == "gene.body")[["target.genes"]],
  FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k27.gene.body) <- NULL
length(k27.gene.body)

## Genes with H3K27me3 overlapping their TSS
k27.tss <- unique(unlist(sapply(
  X = subset(k27.consensus.peak.annotation, 
             peak.annotation == "TSS")[["target.genes"]],
  FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k27.tss) <- NULL
length(k27.tss)

## Genes with H3K27me3 overlapping their TES
k27.tes <- unique(unlist(sapply(
  X = subset(k27.consensus.peak.annotation, 
             peak.annotation == "TES")[["target.genes"]], 
  FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k27.tes) <- NULL
length(k27.tes)

## Genes with H3K27 inside their gene body with no overlap
## in the TSS or TES.
k27.internal.gene.body <- unique(unlist(sapply(
  X = subset(k27.consensus.peak.annotation, 
             peak.annotation == "internal.gene.body")[["target.genes"]],
  FUN = function(x) {strsplit(x,",")[[1]]})))
names(k27.internal.gene.body) <- NULL
k27.internal.gene.body <- setdiff(k27.internal.gene.body,c(k27.tss,k27.tes))
length(k27.internal.gene.body)

```
We found 994 genes associated to H3K27me3 marks corresponding to 13% of the 
entire Ostreococcus genome. H3K27me3 is mostly located occupying either the 
entire gene body (19.6%, 314 genes) or internal regions of gene body (52.8%, 
433 genes). Although some regions occupied by H3K27me3 has been found 
overlapping only with the TSS (4.5%, 49 genes) or the TES (18.8%, 198 genes).
H3K27me3 was found in intergenic regions only in 4.3% of the cases. 

In what follows we perform a functional analysis over the H3K27me3 consensus
marked genes. First, we analyze the relationship between H3K27me3 consensus 
peaks and transposable elements. 

```{r transposable_elements}
dna.transposons <- 
  read.table(file="../te_analysis/dna_transposons_unsorted.bed",
             sep="\t",header=F)
nrow(dna.transposons)

ltr.transposons <- 
  read.table(file="../te_analysis/ltr_transposons_unsorted.bed",
             sep="\t", header=F)
nrow(ltr.transposons)

unclassified.transposons <- 
  read.table(file="../te_analysis/unknown_transposons_unsorted.bed", 
             sep="\t",header = F)
nrow(unclassified.transposons)

overlapping.peaks <- function(target.peak, peaks)
{
 subset(peaks, V1 == target.peak[1] & (
             (V2 >= target.peak[2] & V2 <= target.peak[3]) |
             (V3 >= target.peak[2] & V3 <= target.peak[3]) |
             (V2 <= target.peak[2] & V3 >= target.peak[3])))
}


peak.te <- vector(mode = "character",length = nrow(k27.consensus.peak.annotation))

for(i in 1:nrow(k27.consensus.peak.annotation))
{
 current.peak <- unlist(k27.consensus.peak.annotation[i,1:3])
 
 if(nrow(overlapping.peaks(current.peak,dna.transposons)) > 0)
 {
  peak.te[i] <- "DNA_transposon"
 } else if (nrow(overlapping.peaks(current.peak,ltr.transposons)) > 0)
 {
  peak.te[i] <- "LTR_transposon"
 } else if (nrow(overlapping.peaks(current.peak,unclassified.transposons)) > 0)
 {
  peak.te[i] <- "Unclassified_transposon"
 } else
 {
  peak.te[i] <- "No_transposon"
 }
}

100*table(peak.te)/sum(table(peak.te))

pie(table(peak.te), col=c("black","grey","white","lightblue"))

nrow(dna.transposons)
100*table(peak.te)["DNA_transposon"]/nrow(dna.transposons)

nrow(ltr.transposons)
100*table(peak.te)["LTR_transposon"]/nrow(ltr.transposons)

nrow(unclassified.transposons)
100*table(peak.te)["Unclassified_transposon"]/nrow(unclassified.transposons)


table(k27.consensus.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "DNA_transposon"])
table(k27.consensus.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "LTR_transposon"])
table(k27.consensus.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "Unclassified_transposon"])

table(k27.consensus.peak.annotation$peak.annotation)

(table(k27.consensus.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "DNA_transposon"])["intergenic"] +
table(k27.consensus.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "LTR_transposon"])["intergenic"] +
table(k27.consensus.peak.annotation$peak.annotation[peak.te == "Unclassified_transposon"])["intergenic"]) / table(k27.consensus.peak.annotation$peak.annotation)["intergenic"]

k27.consensus.peak.annotation <- cbind(k27.consensus.peak.annotation,peak.te)
colnames(k27.consensus.peak.annotation)[1:3] <- c("chr","start","end")
write.table(x = k27.consensus.peak.annotation,file = "tables/H3K27me3_consensus_peak_annotation.tsv",quote = F,sep = "\t",row.names = F)
```

H3K27me3 is only partially associated with Transposable Elements. More than 88.4% 
of the peaks did not overlap with any TE. Only 1.1%, 0.6% and 9.9% of the 
H3K27me3 peaks were found overlapping with DNA, LTR and unclassified
transposons respectively. Most TE were neither associated with H3K27me3 peaks, 
specifically 12 out of 35 (34.3%) DNA transposons, 6 out of 69 (8.7%) LTR 
transposons and 104 out of 988 (10.5%) unclassified transposons were H3K27me3 
marked. Nonetheless, most H3K27me3 marks located at intergenic regions (71.1%) 
were associated with transposons.    


```{r k27_go_terms}
library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(org.Otauriv5.eg.db)
k27.go.terms <- enrichGO(gene = all.k27.genes, pvalueCutoff = 1,

                         ont = "BP",

            quote = F,sep = "\t",row.names = F)



```

Our GO enrichment analysis suggests that H3K27me3 is repressing the assembly of
bounded cellular projection, microtubule-based movement and transcription
regulation. Other processes are also significantly affected such as fatty acid 
metabolism and cell differentiation.

We determine the H3K27me3 peaks that significantly change their ChIP signal as 
as response to temperature and the corresponding differentially H3k27me3 marked
genes.

```{r pca_chip_signal}
log2.chip.signal <- log2(chip.signal)

library(limma)
limma.experimental.design <- model.matrix(~ -1+factor(c(1,1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,4,5,5,5,6,6,6)))
colnames(limma.experimental.design) <- c("LDZT8","LDZT16",
                                         "LL10","LL14","LL20","LL26")

linear.fit <- lmFit(log2.chip.signal, limma.experimental.design)

contrast.matrix <- makeContrasts(LDZT16-LDZT8,
                                 LL26-LL10,
                                 LL20-LL10,
                                 LL14-LL10, 
                                 levels = c("LDZT8","LDZT16","LL10","LL14","LL20","LL26"))

contrast.linear.fit <- contrasts.fit(linear.fit, contrast.matrix)
contrast.results <- eBayes(contrast.linear.fit)                               

zt16.zt8 <- topTable(contrast.results, 
                     number=nrow(log2.chip.signal), 
                     coef = 1, sort.by = "logFC") 

write.table(x = zt16.zt8,file = "tables/diff_peaks_zt16_zt8.tsv",
            quote = F,sep ="\t")

zt16.zt8.logfc <- zt16.zt8$logFC
zt16.zt8.adj.p.val <- zt16.zt8$adj.P.Val
zt16.zt8.peak.ids <- rownames(zt16.zt8)

zt16.zt8.higher.peaks <- zt16.zt8.peak.ids[zt16.zt8.logfc > log2(1) & 
                                           zt16.zt8.adj.p.val < 0.05]

zt16.zt8.lower.peaks <- zt16.zt8.peak.ids[zt16.zt8.logfc < -log2(1) & 
                                             zt16.zt8.adj.p.val < 0.05]



t26.t10 <- topTable(contrast.results, 
                     number=nrow(log2.chip.signal), 
                     coef = 2, sort.by = "logFC") 

write.table(x = t26.t10,file = "tables/diff_peaks_26c_10c.tsv",
            quote = F,sep ="\t")

t26.t10.logfc <- t26.t10$logFC
t26.t10.adj.p.val <- t26.t10$adj.P.Val

names(t26.t10.logfc) <- t26.t10.peak.ids
names(t26.t10.adj.p.val) <- t26.t10.peak.ids

t26.t10.higher.peaks <- t26.t10.peak.ids[t26.t10.logfc > log2(1.5) & 
                                           t26.t10.adj.p.val < 0.01]

t26.t10.lower.peaks <- t26.t10.peak.ids[t26.t10.logfc < -log2(1.5) &

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_chip_signal_volcano_26_10.jpg",res = 160,width = 750,height = 750)

     pch=20,xlim=c(-3,3),ylim=c(0,8),cex.axis=1.5,col="grey",
     xlab="log2(fc)",ylab="-log10(p.val)",cex.lab=1.5)
points(x = t26.t10.logfc[t26.t10.higher.peaks],y = -log10(t26.t10.adj.p.val)[t26.t10.higher.peaks],
     pch=20,xlim=c(-3,3),ylim=c(0,8),cex.axis=1.5,cex=1.5,col="yellow")
```

Over 40.8% of the H3K27me3 marked genes significantly increase more than 50% 
their H3K27me3 ChIP signal as a response to temperature and 5.8% significantly 
decrease their H3K27me3 ChIP signal.


```{r chip_signal_gradual_change}
chip.signal.10C <- rowMeans(chip.signal[,paste("t10C",1:3,sep="_")])
chip.signal.14C <- rowMeans(chip.signal[,paste("t14C",1:3,sep="_")])
chip.signal.20C <- rowMeans(chip.signal[,paste("t20C",1:3,sep="_")])
chip.signal.26C <- rowMeans(chip.signal[,paste("t26C",1:3,sep="_")])

#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_higher.jpg",res = 160,width = 750,height = 900)
boxplot(chip.signal.10C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
        chip.signal.14C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
        chip.signal.20C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
        chip.signal.26C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
        outline=F,
        names=c("10ºC","14ºC","20ºC","26ºC"),
        col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(4),lwd=2,cex.axis=1.5)
#dev.off()

wilcox.test(x = chip.signal.10C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
            y = chip.signal.14C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
            alternative = "less",paired = T)


wilcox.test(x = chip.signal.14C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
            y = chip.signal.20C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
            alternative = "less",paired = T)$p.value

wilcox.test(x = chip.signal.20C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
            y = chip.signal.26C[k27.temp.higher.peaks],
            alternative = "less",paired = T)$p.value


#jpeg(filename = "images/h3k27me3_lower.jpg",res = 160,width = 750,height = 900)
boxplot(chip.signal.10C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
        chip.signal.14C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
        chip.signal.20C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
        chip.signal.26C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
        outline=F,
        names=c("10ºC","14ºC","20ºC","26ºC"),
        col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(4),lwd=2,cex.axis=1.5)
#dev.off()

wilcox.test(x = chip.signal.10C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
            y = chip.signal.14C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
            alternative = "greater",paired = T)


wilcox.test(x = chip.signal.14C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
            y = chip.signal.20C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
            alternative = "greater",paired = T)

wilcox.test(x = chip.signal.20C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
            y = chip.signal.26C[k27.temp.lower.peaks],
            alternative = "greater",paired = T)

```
We observe a temperature dependent gradual increase in the higher peaks. This
increase is significant according to wilcox test with p values of 5.2x10^-6^
between 10ºC and 14ºC, 1.6x10^-60^ between 14ºC and 20ºC and 4.1x10^-67^ 
between 20ºC and 24ºC. 

Similarly in the lower peaks, we observe a temperature dependent gradual 
decrease. This decrease is significant according to wilcox text with p values
of 1.9x10^-9^ between 10ºC and 14ºC, 1.1x10^-5^ between 14ºC and 20 and no 
significant difference between 20ºC and 26ºC.

```{r gene_expression_analysis}
library(DESeq2)

## Load the gene expression estimation based on read count. 
gene.count.matrix <- read.table(file = "gene_expression_data/gene_count_matrix.csv",header = T,sep = ",")
head(gene.count.matrix)

## Extract gene ids in the order present in the gene count matrix
deseq.gene.ids <- gene.count.matrix$gene_id

## Generate a numerical matrix by removing the first columns with gene names. 
gene.count.matrix <- gene.count.matrix[,-1]
rownames(gene.count.matrix) <- deseq.gene.ids
colnames(gene.count.matrix) <- colnames(gene.expression)
head(gene.count.matrix)

experimental.design <- data.frame(sample=colnames(gene.expression),
                                  temperature=c(rep("t10C",3),
                                          rep("t14C",3),
                                          rep("t20C",3),
                                          rep("t26C",3)))


## Generate object needed by DESeq2 to perform DEGs analysis
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData=gene.count.matrix, 
                              colData=experimental.design, 
                              design = ~ temperature)

## Perfom DEGs analysis
dds <- DESeq(dds) 

## Extract results for comparison treatment=14C and control=t10C 
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("temperature","t14C","t10C")) 
res

## Extract gene ids, log2 fc and q-value for this comparison
gene.ids.14.vs.10 <- rownames(res)
log.fold.change <- res$log2FoldChange
adjusted.pval <- res$padj

## Name the vectors with the gene ids
names(log.fold.change) <- gene.ids.14.vs.10
names(adjusted.pval) <- gene.ids.14.vs.10

## Determine activated and repressed genes removing NA
activated.genes.14.vs.10 <- gene.ids.14.vs.10[log.fold.change > 1 & 
                                               adjusted.pval < 0.05]
activated.genes.14.vs.10 <- activated.genes.14.vs.10[!is.na(activated.genes.14.vs.10)]
length(activated.genes.14.vs.10)
```

We found 751 genes that significantly increase more than twice their expression
as a response to temperature and 138 genes that significantly decrease more than
half their expression as a response to temperature. 

Next we study the expression level of H3K27me3 genes that significantly increase
their ChIP signal as a response to temperature more than 50%.

We identified 134 genes that, in response to high temperature, exhibited 
a more than 50% significant increase in H3K27me3 ChIP signal and a greater than
twofold reduction in expression levels. These genes represent 17.8% of the total
set of genes that showed significant downregulation in response to temperature 
increase. The overlap between genes with a significantl increase in H3K27me3 
ChIP signal and those significantly downregulated is highly significant with a 
p-value of 1.15x10^-40^. This suggests that H3K27me3 plays a key role in 
temperature response being involved in the regulation of nearly  18% of the 
differentially repressed genes.


Next we explore the biological processes affected by changes in H3K27me3 as
a response to temperature.

The following two functions are used to represent the ChIP signal and expression 
level for specific genes. 

```{r chip_signal_and_expression}
gene.profile.complete <- function(gene.name, 
                         promoter_length=1000, 
                         selected.bigwig.files,
                         cols,
                         selected.bed.files)
{
  target.gene.body <- genes.data.df[gene.name,]
  target.gene.chr <- as.character(target.gene.body$seqnames)
  target.gene.start <- target.gene.body$start
  target.gene.end <- target.gene.body$end
  
  target.gene.strand <- as.character(target.gene.body$strand)
  
  ## Extract cds annotation
  cds.data.target.gene <- subset(cds.data, 
                                 seqnames == target.gene.chr & 
                                   (start >= target.gene.start & 
                                      end <= target.gene.end))
  
  ## Extract exons annotation
  exons.data.target.gene <- subset(exons.data, 
                                   seqnames == target.gene.chr & 
                                     (start >= target.gene.start & 
                                        end <= target.gene.end))
  
  ## Determine the genome range to plot including promoter, gene body and 5' UTR
  ## This depends on whether the gene is on the forward or reverse strand
  range.to.plot <- target.gene.body
  
  if(target.gene.strand == "+")
  {
    range.to.plot$start <- range.to.plot$start - promoter_length
    range.to.plot$end <- range.to.plot$end + promoter_length
  } else if (target.gene.strand == "-")
  {
    range.to.plot$end <- range.to.plot$end + promoter_length
    range.to.plot$start <- range.to.plot$start - promoter_length
  }
  
  ## Compute the length of the genome range to represent
  current.length <- range.to.plot$end - range.to.plot$start
  
  ## Compute profile in gene
  ## Since ChIPpeakAnno needs more than one region to plot our region
  ## is duplicated 
  regions.plot <- GRanges(rbind(range.to.plot,range.to.plot))
  
  ## Import signal from the bigwig files
  cvglists <- sapply(selected.bigwig.files, import, 
                     format="BigWig", 
                     which=regions.plot, 
                     as="RleList")
  
  ## Compute signal in the region to plot
  chip.signal <- featureAlignedSignal(cvglists, regions.plot, 
                                      upstream=ceiling(current.length/2), 
                                      downstream=ceiling(current.length/2),
                                      n.tile=current.length) 
  
  
  
  chip.signal[[1]][1:2,1:5]
  
  
  chip.signal.mean <- matrix(nrow=length(selected.bigwig.files),ncol=dim(chip.signal[[1]])[2])

  ## Compute mean signal 
  for(i in 1:length(selected.bigwig.files))
  {
    if(target.gene.strand == "+")
    {
      chip.signal.mean[i,] <- colMeans(chip.signal[[i]],na.rm = TRUE)
    } else if (target.gene.strand == "-")
    {
      chip.signal.mean[i,] <- rev(colMeans(chip.signal[[i]],na.rm = TRUE))
    }
  }
  
  ## Normalization
  #chip.signal.mean <- 20 * chip.signal.mean / max(chip.signal.mean)
  upper.lim <- 1.1*max(chip.signal.mean)
  ## Colors to draw signal
  line.colors <- cols[i]#"blue"
  area.colors <- cols[i]#"lightblue"
  
  gene.height <- -25
  cord.x <- 1:current.length
  
  ## Exon width to plot
  exon.width <- 2#1#2
  
  ## Cds width to plot
  cds.width <- 3#1.5#3
  
  ## Width of the rectangule representing the peak reagion
  peak.width <- 1#0.5#1
  
  ## Extract exons for target gene
  exons.data.target.gene <- subset(exons.data, seqnames == target.gene.chr & (start >= target.gene.start & end <= target.gene.end))
  
  ## Transform exon coordinates to current range
  min.pos <- min(exons.data.target.gene$start)
  
  exons.data.target.gene$start <- exons.data.target.gene$start - min.pos + promoter_length
  exons.data.target.gene$end <- exons.data.target.gene$end - min.pos + promoter_length
  
  ## Extract cds for target gene
  cds.data.target.gene <- subset(cds.data, seqnames == target.gene.chr & (start >= target.gene.start & end <= target.gene.end))
  
  cds.data.target.gene$start <- cds.data.target.gene$start - min.pos + promoter_length
  cds.data.target.gene$end <- cds.data.target.gene$end - min.pos + promoter_length
  
  plot(cord.x, rep(gene.height,length(cord.x)),type="l",col="black",lwd=3,ylab="",
       cex.lab=2,axes=FALSE,xlab="",main="",cex.main=2,
       ylim=c(-35,upper.lim),xlim=c(0,max(cord.x)))
  
  ## Represent exons
  for(i in 1:nrow(exons.data.target.gene))
  {
    # Determine start/end for each exon
    current.exon.start <- exons.data.target.gene$start[i]
    current.exon.end <- exons.data.target.gene$end[i]
    
    ## Determine coordinates for each exon polygon and represent it
    exon.x <- c(current.exon.start,current.exon.end,current.exon.end,current.exon.start)
    exon.y <- c(gene.height + exon.width, gene.height + exon.width, gene.height - exon.width, gene.height - exon.width)
    
    polygon(x = exon.x, y = exon.y, col = "blue",border = "blue")
  }
  
  if(nrow(cds.data.target.gene) > 0)
  {
    for(i in 1:nrow(cds.data.target.gene))
    {
      # Determine current cds start/end
      current.cds.start <- cds.data.target.gene$start[i]
      current.cds.end <- cds.data.target.gene$end[i]
      
      # Determine curret cds coordinates for the polygon and represent it
      cds.x <- c(current.cds.start,current.cds.end,current.cds.end,current.cds.start)
      cds.y <- c(gene.height + cds.width, gene.height + cds.width, gene.height - cds.width, gene.height - cds.width)
      polygon(x = cds.x, y = cds.y, col = "blue",border = "blue")
    }
  }
  
  ## Draw arrow to represent transcription direction 
  if(target.gene.strand == "+")
  {
    lines(c(promoter_length,promoter_length,promoter_length+100),
          y=c(gene.height,gene.height+5,gene.height+5),lwd=3)
    lines(c(promoter_length+50,promoter_length+100),y=c(gene.height+6,gene.height+5),lwd=3)
    lines(c(promoter_length+50,promoter_length+100),y=c(gene.height+4,gene.height+5),lwd=3)
  } else if (target.gene.strand == "-")
  {
    lines(c(current.length - promoter_length, current.length - promoter_length, current.length - promoter_length-100),y=c(gene.height,gene.height+5,gene.height+5),lwd=3)
    lines(c(current.length - promoter_length-50, current.length - promoter_length - 100),y=c(gene.height + 6, gene.height + 5),lwd=3)
    lines(c(current.length - promoter_length-50, current.length - promoter_length - 100),y=c(gene.height + 4, gene.height + 5),lwd=3)
  }
  
  ## Draw promoter range
  if(target.gene.strand == "+")
  {
    axis(side = 1,labels = c(- promoter_length, - promoter_length / 2,"TSS"),at = c(1,promoter_length/2,promoter_length),lwd=2,cex=1.5,las=2,cex=2)
  } else if(target.gene.strand == "-")
  {
    axis(side = 1,labels = c("TSS",- promoter_length / 2,- promoter_length),at = c(current.length-promoter_length,current.length-promoter_length/2, current.length),lwd=2,cex=1.5,las=2,cex=2)
  }
  
  ## Draw gene name
  text(x = current.length / 2, y = -33 , 
       labels = bquote(italic(.(gene.name))),cex = 1.7,font = 3)
  
  ## Extract bed file name 1 and read it
  current.peaks <- read.table(file=selected.bed.files,header = F, as.is = T)
  current.peaks <- current.peaks[,1:3]
  colnames(current.peaks) <- c("seqnames","start","end")
  peak.coordinates <- subset(current.peaks, seqnames == as.character(range.to.plot$seqnames) & start >= range.to.plot$start & end <= range.to.plot$end) 
  current.peaks.to.plot <- peak.coordinates[,2:3]
  
  ## Transform coordinates 
  current.peaks.to.plot <- current.peaks.to.plot - range.to.plot$start
  
  ## Check if there are peaks for the target gene
  if(nrow(current.peaks.to.plot) > 0)
  {
    #motifs.in.peaks <- vector(mode="list", length=nrow(current.peaks.to.plot))
    for(j in 1:nrow(current.peaks.to.plot))
    {
      ## Extract start and end point of each peak region
      current.peak.start <- current.peaks.to.plot[j,1]
      current.peak.end <- current.peaks.to.plot[j,2]
      
      ## Computer coordinates for polygon and draw it
      peak.x <- c(current.peak.start,current.peak.end,
                  current.peak.end,current.peak.start)
      peak.y <- c(peak.width - 12,   peak.width - 12, 
                  - peak.width - 12, - peak.width - 12)  
      
      polygon(x = peak.x, y = peak.y, col = "blue", border = "blue",lwd=2)
    }
  }
  
  ## Draw profiles if bw file is provided
  ## Compute base line for current TF
  current.base.line <- - 10
  
  i <- 4
  
  for(i in 1:length(selected.bigwig.files))
  {
    ## Represent signal from the current TF
    lines(chip.signal.mean[i,]+current.base.line,type="l",col=cols[i],lwd=3)
    ## Determine polygon coordinates and represent it
    cord.y <- c(current.base.line,chip.signal.mean[i,]+current.base.line,current.base.line)
    cord.x <- 1:length(cord.y)
    polygon(cord.x,cord.y,col=cols[i])
  }
  
  axis(side = 2,lwd = 2,
       at = seq(from=0,to=ceiling(upper.lim/10)*10,by=10)+current.base.line,
       labels = seq(from=0,to=ceiling(upper.lim/10)*10,by=10))
}

gene.expression.barplot <- function(gene.id, gene.expression)
{
  gene.expression.10 <- unlist(gene.expression[gene.id,paste("t10C",1:3,sep="_")])
  gene.expression.14 <- unlist(gene.expression[gene.id,paste("t14C",1:3,sep="_")])
  gene.expression.20 <- unlist(gene.expression[gene.id,paste("t20C",1:3,sep="_")])
  gene.expression.26 <- unlist(gene.expression[gene.id,paste("t26C",1:3,sep="_")])
  
  means <- c(mean(gene.expression.10),
             mean(gene.expression.14),
             mean(gene.expression.20),
             mean(gene.expression.26))
  
  sds <- c(sd(gene.expression.10),
           sd(gene.expression.14),
           sd(gene.expression.20),
           sd(gene.expression.26))
  
  y.max <- 1.2*max(means + sds)
  
  par(lwd=2)
  xpos <- barplot(means,ylim=c(0,y.max),
                  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(4),cex.axis = 1.5,
                  names.arg = c("10ºC","14ºC","20ºC","26ºC"),cex.names=2,lwd=2)
  par(lwd=1)
  arrows(x0 = xpos,y0 = means-sds/sqrt(3), x1 = xpos,y1=means+sds/sqrt(3),code=3,angle=90,length=0.07,lwd=2)
  
  
  points(x = rep(xpos+0.2,each=3),y=c(gene.expression.10,
                                      gene.expression.14,
                                      gene.expression.20,
                                      gene.expression.26),lwd=2)
  
}


```

Kinesins are involved in long range vesicle transport through microtubules and 
myosing are involved in short range transport through actin filaments. Kinesins 
(microtubules) and myosins (actin filaments) combination suggests a two-phase 
vesicle transport system activated at low temperatures. Long-range transport 
along microtubules by kinesins followed by short-range delivery to the membrane 
along the cortical actin network by myosins.

Although no significant enrichment was found for lipid metabolism in the genes
that significantly increase their H3K27me3 ChIP-signal and decrease their 
expression level, key genes in lipid metabolism and transport were identified
in this set of genes: enoyl-ACP reductase (ENR, ostta17g00300), diacylglycerol
acyltransferase (DGAT, ostta16g00910) and ABC type 2 transporter (ABC, 
ostta09g01615).
