## Evolutionary comparison of H3K27me3 genes in Ostreococcus tauri and Arabidopsis thaliana

We compare according to orthology relationships the H3K27me3 marked genes found
in Ostreococcus tauri in this study with those found in Arabidopsis thaliana in
our previous study "H2A monoubiquitination in Arabidopsis thaliana is generally 
independent of LHP1 and PRC2 activity. Zhou Y, Romero-Campero FJ, Gómez-Zambrano 
Á, Turck F, Calonje M. Genome Biol. 2017 Apr 12;18(1):69. 
doi: 10.1186/s13059-017-1197-z.". 

First, we load the H3K27me3 marked genes in Arabidopsis thaliana:

```{r load_genes}
atha.k27.genes <- unique(c(read.table(file="h3k27me3_h2aub_atha.txt",header = F,as.is=T)[[1]],
                    read.table(file="only_h3k27me3_atha.txt",header = F,as.is=T)[[1]]))
length(atha.k27.genes)
length(atha.k27.genes)/34100
length(all.k27.genes)
length(all.k27.genes)/7668
```

H3k27me3 marks are found in 6843 genes in Arabidopsis accounting for 20% of its
entire genome, compared to the 994 genes associated to H3K27me3 marks 
corresponding to 13% of the entire Ostreococcus genome. H3K27me3 has been shown
to associate primarly with developmental genes rather than TE being 
H3K9me2/H3K29me3 the main repressive epigenetic mark for transposable elements. 
Nonetheless, some autonomous TE near genes have been found marked by H3K27me3 
specially in euchromatic regions in Arabidopsis. In our study we have found a 
similar role for H3K27me3 in Ostreococcus tauri. In our pico alga this mark also
associate primarly with non TE although some TEs are found to be H3K27me3 marked. 

In order to determine in the H3K27me3 marked genes in Arabidopsis and Ostreococcus
are evolutionarily related we load gene orthology relationships as orthogropus 
between all the genes in Ostreococcus tauri and Arabidopsis thaliana genomes.
Then we determine the orthogroups form each species containing at least one
H3K27me3 marked genes to determine H3K27me3 marked orthogroups that are 
compared using a Venn diagram. 

```{r h3k27me3_orthogroups}
ostta.atha.orthogroups <- read.table(file="ostta_atha_orthogroups.tsv",header=T,sep="\t")
ostta.atha.orthogroups <- subset(ostta.atha.orthogroups, 
                                 ostreococcus_tauri != "" | arabidopsis_thaliana != "")
nrow(ostta.atha.orthogroups)

number.orthogroups <- nrow(ostta.atha.orthogroups)
ostta.orthogroups <- c()
for(i in 1:length(all.k27.genes))
{
#  print(i)
  current.gene <- all.k27.genes[[i]]
  
  j <- 1
  while(j < number.orthogroups & !current.gene %in% 
        strsplit(x = ostta.atha.orthogroups$ostreococcus_tauri[[j]],
                 split = ", ")[[1]])
  {
    j <- j + 1
  }
  
  if(current.gene %in% 
     strsplit(x = ostta.atha.orthogroups$ostreococcus_tauri[[j]],
              split = ", ")[[1]])
  {
    ostta.orthogroups <- c(ostta.orthogroups, 
                           ostta.atha.orthogroups$Orthogroup[j]) 
  }
}
ostta.orthogroups <-  unique(ostta.orthogroups)
length(ostta.orthogroups)

atha.orthogroups <- c()
for(i in 1:length(atha.k27.genes))
{
#  print(i)
  current.gene <- atha.k27.genes[[i]]
  
  j <- 1
  while(j < number.orthogroups & !current.gene %in% 
        strsplit(x = ostta.atha.orthogroups$arabidopsis_thaliana[[j]],
                 split = ", ")[[1]])
  {
    j <- j + 1
  }
  
  if(current.gene %in% 
     strsplit(x = ostta.atha.orthogroups$arabidopsis_thaliana[[j]],
              split = ", ")[[1]])
  {
    atha.orthogroups <- c(atha.orthogroups, 
                           ostta.atha.orthogroups$Orthogroup[j]) 
  }
}
length(atha.orthogroups)
atha.orthogroups <-  unique(atha.orthogroups)
length(atha.orthogroups)

all.k27.ostta.atha <- intersect(ostta.orthogroups,atha.orthogroups)

#jpeg(filename = "images/venn_diagram_k27_ostta_atha.jpg",res = 160,width = 1000,height = 1000)
grid.newpage()
draw.pairwise.venn(area1 = length(ostta.orthogroups),
                   area2 = length(atha.orthogroups),
                   cross.area =  length(all.k27.ostta.atha),
                   lwd = 5,category = c("",""),
                   euler.d = T,
                   col = c("darkgreen","green"),
                   fill = c("darkgreen","green"),
                   alpha = 0.5,cex = 3,cat.cex = 2)
#dev.off()
overlap <- length(all.k27.ostta.atha)
size.1 <- length(ostta.orthogroups)
size.2 <- length(atha.orthogroups)
total.orthogroups <- nrow(ostta.atha.orthogroups)
phyper(overlap - 1, size.1, total.orthogroups - size.1, size.2, lower.tail = FALSE)

sum(subset(ostta.atha.orthogroups, Orthogroup %in% ostta.specific.k27.orthogroups)$arabidopsis_thaliana != "")/length(ostta.specific.k27.orthogroups)
sum(subset(ostta.atha.orthogroups, Orthogroup %in% atha.specific.k27.orthogroups)$ostreococcus_tauri != "")/length(atha.specific.k27.orthogroups)
```

We found 749 Ostreococcus tauri orthogroups and 1859 Arabidopsis thaliana 
orthogroups with at least one H3K27me3 marked gene in the corresponding 
species. These orthogroups will be referred to as H3K27me3 marked orthogroups. 
Only a non significant overlap consisting of 77 orthogroups was
identified as commonly H3K27me3 marked in both species. 52% of the Ostreococcus
tauri specifically H3K27me3 marked orthogroups posses Arabidopsis thaliana
representatives. Viceversa

This indicates that although during evolution new gene families represented by
orthogroups have emerged in Arabidopsis and have been 

This indicates that 
H3K27me3 regulates very different biological processes in both species.

Next we explore the commonly H3K27me3 marked orthogroups in both species using
GO and KEGG term enrichment analysis.

```{r enrichment_h3k27me3_ostta_atha_orthogroups}
ostta.k27.ostta.atha <- intersect(unlist(strsplit(x = subset(ostta.atha.orthogroups, Orthogroup %in% all.k27.ostta.atha)$ostreococcus_tauri,split=", ")),all.k27.genes)

ostta.k27.ostta.atha.go.terms <- enrichGO(gene = ostta.k27.ostta.atha, pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                         qvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                         OrgDb = org.Otauriv5.eg.db,
                         ont = "BP", 
                         keyType = "GID")
write.table(x = as.data.frame(ostta.k27.ostta.atha.go.terms),file="tables/go_enrichment_ostta_common_marked_orthogroups.tsv",quote = F,sep = "\t")

jpeg(filename = "images/go_ostta_common_k27_orthogroups.jpg",res = 120,width = 1300,height = 500)
treeplot(x = pairwise_termsim(ostta.k27.ostta.atha.go.terms),cluster.params = list(n = 2))
dev.off()

library(org.At.tair.db)
atha.k27.ostta.atha <- intersect(unlist(strsplit(x = subset(ostta.atha.orthogroups, Orthogroup %in% all.k27.ostta.atha)$arabidopsis_thaliana,split=", ")), atha.k27.genes)
atha.k27.ostta.atha.go.terms <- enrichGO(gene = atha.k27.ostta.atha, pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                                          qvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                                          OrgDb = org.At.tair.db,
                                          ont = "BP", 
                                          keyType = "TAIR")
write.table(x = as.data.frame(atha.k27.ostta.atha.go.terms),file="tables/go_enrichment_atha_common_marked_orthogroups.tsv",quote = F,sep = "\t")

#jpeg(filename = "images/go_atha_common_k27_orthogroups.jpg",res = 120,width = 1300,height = 500)
treeplot(x = pairwise_termsim(atha.k27.ostta.atha.go.terms),cluster.params = list(n = 2))
#dev.off()
```


Next we explore the Ostreococcus tauri specific H3K27me3 marked orthogroups 
using GO and KEGG term enrichment analysis.

```{r enrichment_h3k27me3_ostta_specific_orthogroups}
ostta.specific.k27.orthogroups <- setdiff(ostta.orthogroups,atha.orthogroups)
length(ostta.specific.k27.orthogroups)
sum(subset(ostta.atha.orthogroups, Orthogroup %in% ostta.specific.k27.orthogroups)$arabidopsis_thaliana != "")/length(ostta.specific.k27.orthogroups)

ostta.specific.k27 <- unlist(strsplit(x = subset(ostta.atha.orthogroups, Orthogroup %in% ostta.specific.k27.orthogroups)$ostreococcus_tauri,split=", "))

ostta.specific.k27.go.terms <- enrichGO(gene = intersect(all.k27.genes,ostta.specific.k27), pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                                       qvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                                       OrgDb = org.Otauriv5.eg.db,
                                       ont = "BP", 
                                       keyType = "GID")
write.table(x = as.data.frame(ostta.specific.k27.go.terms),file="tables/go_enrichment_ostta_specific_marked_orthogroups.tsv",quote = F,sep = "\t")
#jpeg(filename = "images/go_ostta_specific_k27_orthogroups.jpg",res = 120,width = 1300,height = 500)
treeplot(x = pairwise_termsim(ostta.specific.k27.go.terms),cluster.params = list(n = 2))
#dev.off()
```
We identified 672 orthogroups only marked in Ostreococcus tauri. 52.2% of these
orthogroups also contained Arabidopsis genes. Therefore the reason why these
orthogroups are specific to Ostreococcus is not related to the absence of 
Arabidopsis genes in them. This indicates that H3K273me3 regulates specific
processes in Ostreococcus that are not regulated in Arabidopsis. Among these 
Ostreococus tauri H3K27me3 specific biological processes we highlight:

* DNA integration with H3K27me3 marked genes like the integrase codified by
ostta11g02575 and the reverse transcriptase ostta19g00515. 

```{r k27_dna_integration}
#jpeg(filename = "images/INT_ostta11g02575.jpg",res = 100,width = 600,height = 580)
gene.profile.complete(gene.name = "ostta11g02575",
                      promoter_length=1000, 
                      selected.bigwig.files = c("h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_26_chip_2.bw",
                                                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_10_chip_2.bw",
                                                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_10_chip_2.bw",
                                                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_10_chip_2.bw"),
                      cols = rev(colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(4)),
                      selected.bed.files = "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_peaks.bed")
#dev.off()

gene.expression.barplot(gene.id = "ostta11g02575", gene.expression=gene.expression)

gene.profile.complete(gene.name = "ostta19g00515",
                      promoter_length=1000, 
                      selected.bigwig.files = c("h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_26_chip_2.bw",
                                                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_10_chip_2.bw",
                                                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_10_chip_2.bw",
                                                "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_ll_10_chip_2.bw"),

                      selected.bed.files = "h3k27me3/h3k27me3_peaks.bed")

gene.expression.barplot(gene.id = "ostta19g00515", gene.expression=gene.expression)
```

* Meiotic cell cycle with H3K27me3 marked genes specifically involved in the
pachytene stage of meiosis particularly ostta11g01720 (Disrupted Meiotic cDNA 1,
DMC1), ostta07g03600 (meiotic recombination protein SPO22) and ostta05g02370
(Pachytene Associated Protein 2, PA2). These proteins mediate chromosome 
remodeling and crossover by homologous recombination.
